items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section X, List of Answers on Terminology 29:1
items.html: It is known that every illumination comes from Ein Sof [infinity] and passes through all the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] until it arrives at the receiver. For example, when ZON receive some illumination, it comes from Ein Sof and passes through all five Partzufim of AK and the first three Partzufim of Atzilut, and only then does it come to ZON. It is also known that every phase receives only from the phase corresponding to it in the upper Partzufim. Accordingly, Zeir and Nukva, for example, do not receive from all the Partzufim that precede them, but only from the phases within them that correspond to them. The matter is that in truth ZON must receive its illumination through all the phases in the Partzufim that precede it. However, there is a difference: from those phases in the upper ones that are not related to its own phase, it receives by way of passage, meaning that the abundance is not clothed at all in the corrections that they have. But when the abundance passes through the phases that correspond to it in the upper Partzufim, the abundance is clothed in the corrections found in those phases in the upper ones. Thus, apart from the abundance itself, which it receives from Ein Sof, it also receives all the corrections found in the phases corresponding to it in the upper ones, up to its own degree. This is called “by way of clothing”. This is not so with the phases that are not related to it: there the abundance passes by way of passage, without taking anything of their corrections. (Page 926, Items 103 and 104).
